hypotheses.H1: Expansion: growing resources and widening public-policy engagement
hypotheses.H2: Consolidation: stable resources, defending a core issue set
hypotheses.H3: Retrenchment: shrinking resources or salience, narrowing engagement
hypotheses.H4: Realignment: shifting issues or partners while resources hold

ach.note: ACH ranks hypotheses by how much evidence contradicts them; it is analyst judgment, not probability. Tie between H1, H4; collect the missing indicators before preferring one.

9d2776e2287b06b6.claim: CCUSA's FY2025 annual report states the network's 169 member agencies served more than 16 million people through 4,230 service sites in all 50 states, D.C. and five U.S. territories; later 2026 releases describe membership as 170 diocesan agencies.
9d2776e2287b06b6.source_title: Called to Serve: Catholic Charities USA 2025 Annual Report

68cc8b7485eeb98d.claim: Network service scale reported for FY2025: more than 30 million meals, 3.2 million nights of emergency shelter, 201,000 people receiving emergency housing services, 64,000 clients trained and placed in jobs, and 108 agencies providing pregnancy support.
68cc8b7485eeb98d.source_title: Called to Serve: Catholic Charities USA 2025 Annual Report

3c11bcc794d57688.claim: Audited FY2025 (year ending June 30, 2025) figures for the national office: total revenue $71.5M, of which contributions were $58.8M, federal grants only $3.0M (about 4%) and membership dues $1.7M; total expenses $56.0M; net assets rose $15.5M. In-kind donations of about $30M are excluded. Analyst note: the national office's low federal dependence insulates it from grant cuts, even though member agencies are more exposed.
3c11bcc794d57688.source_title: Called to Serve: Catholic Charities USA 2025 Annual Report (financial summary)

02c0db994a68b790.claim: After the January 2025 federal freeze on refugee resettlement funding, at least a dozen Catholic Charities agencies from Florida to California laid off hundreds of employees, and some closed their refugee resettlement programs entirely.
02c0db994a68b790.source_title: Catholic Charities agencies halt refugee programs in wake of US aid freeze (National Catholic Reporter)

2a874e99b580b57f.claim: The State Department terminated the USCCB's refugee resettlement cooperative agreement in February 2025. USCCB, the Catholic partner in the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program whose local resettlement work was carried out largely by diocesan Catholic Charities agencies, agreed to wind down its participation, laid off about a third of its Migration and Refugee Services staff, and voluntarily dismissed its lawsuit in January 2026 after recovering funds it was owed (more than $24M as of April 2025).
2a874e99b580b57f.source_title: US bishops end lawsuit against Trump administration over refugee resettlement (OSV News)

a92838435d4afc9c.claim: In Catholic Charities Bureau, Inc. v. Wisconsin Labor & Industry Review Commission (No. 24-154), the U.S. Supreme Court ruled 9-0 that denying a diocesan Catholic Charities entity a religious unemployment-tax exemption because it neither proselytizes nor serves only Catholics is an unconstitutional denominational preference. The ruling strengthens the legal footing of the network's nonsectarian service model.
a92838435d4afc9c.source_title: Catholic Charities Bureau, Inc. v. Wisconsin Labor & Industry Review Comm'n, 605 U.S. ___ (2025)

f3f2fb81ef75b85c.claim: Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Fort Worth sued HHS in March 2025 (No. 1:25-cv-00605, D.D.C.) over frozen refugee-program funds. After HHS resumed payments (more than $47M was paid following a program-integrity review), the case was dismissed as moot on April 29, 2025. This shows member agencies can use litigation to restore federal payments.
f3f2fb81ef75b85c.source_title: Catholic Charities Diocese of Fort Worth, Inc. v. DHHS (Civil Rights Litigation Clearinghouse)

55b4f98aa8849f6b.claim: On June 11, 2025, the House Homeland Security Committee chair and its oversight subcommittee chair opened an investigation into more than 200 NGOs over taxpayer-funded services to migrants. Catholic Charities USA and USCCB were named among the recipients of document requests.
55b4f98aa8849f6b.source_title: Chairmen Green, Brecheen Launch Probe into 200+ NGOs (House Committee on Homeland Security)

68bbbf412e3a0766.claim: Catholic Charities of the Rio Grande Valley, a member agency, was reported in late 2025 to be suspended from federal funds and facing a six-year debarment after a DHS review of FEMA migrant-shelter grant records. The reports rest on DHS documents shared with Fox News. The agency said it is working to regain eligibility and comply with grant requirements.
68bbbf412e3a0766.source_title: Trump administration freezes federal funding for South Texas migrant shelter (Texas Tribune)

4c9de8a893462e78.claim: At a July 2025 House Homeland Security hearing on NGOs and the border, some Republicans accused Catholic Charities of facilitating illegal immigration, while Democrats and some Republicans defended its work. CCUSA responded by welcoming the 'bipartisan compliments'. Catholic Charities' public salience on immigration is therefore high and polarized.
4c9de8a893462e78.source_title: At tense hearing, GOP attacks immigrant aid groups and fends off accusations of anti-Catholicism (RNS)

40d526f200112c84.claim: Staff at several Catholic Charities agencies (San Diego, Laredo, Southwestern Ohio) received threats after online videos and influencer campaigns targeting their migrant services; Catholic Charities San Diego hired armed guards. These security costs and risks strain local operations.
40d526f200112c84.source_title: Threats to Catholic Charities staffers rise amid far-right anti-migrant campaign (National Catholic Reporter)

bbb704122bdadb00.claim: CCUSA endorsed and lobbied for the ROAD to Housing Act. The final vehicle, H.R. 6644 (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act), passed the House 358-32 on June 23, 2026 and became Public Law 119-101 on July 11, 2026 without the President's signature. CCUSA publicly praised its LIHTC, HOME, CDBG and homelessness-program provisions.
bbb704122bdadb00.source_title: Public Law 119-101 (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act)

28cd907941c01032.claim: CCUSA has retained ArentFox Schiff LLP since at least 2024 ($30,000 reported per quarter), lobbying on BUD, HOU, IMM, TAX and LBR. In Q2 2026 it added a second outside firm, Mercury Public Affairs ($30,000 per quarter), lobbying on REL ('religious freedom'). LDA records show no in-house registration. The Q3 2026 report names the FY2027 Labor-HHS (H.R. 9260), THUD (H.R. 9170), Agriculture (H.R. 8646) and DHS (H.R. 9310) appropriations bills, the Empty Lots to Housing Act (H.R. 3459) and the Reducing Homelessness Through Program Reform Act (S. 2234).
28cd907941c01032.source_title: LDA LD-2 Q3 2026, ArentFox Schiff LLP for Catholic Charities USA

ddb2b379baac2635.claim: CCUSA issues joint positions with peer Catholic institutions. Examples: a November 2026 joint statement with the Catholic Health Association welcoming a federal ruling that blocked CMS Medicaid eligibility guidance, and a May 2025 housing-funding letter to Congress co-signed with USCCB's domestic justice committee chair and the Society of St. Vincent de Paul.
ddb2b379baac2635.source_title: CHA, CCUSA welcome ruling protecting Medicaid access

7cca3be6909cb155.claim: USCCB commissioned CCUSA in 1990 as the Catholic Church's official domestic disaster relief agency. In FY2025, CCUSA worked with 30 agencies on 42 disasters in 19 states, awarded $14.6M in disaster recovery assistance, and spent $22.7M on disaster response, its largest expense line. In October 2026 it opened a Hurricane Isaias relief fund.
7cca3be6909cb155.source_title: Catholic Charities USA launches relief fund for those impacted by Hurricane Isaias

bf44239f47249c62.claim: In 2026, CCUSA launched a multi-phase national advertising campaign across TV, print, digital display, sponsored email, podcast and Spanish-language media. It also began a three-year People of Hope traveling museum tour planned for more than 150 communities, funded by a nearly $5M Lilly Endowment grant.
bf44239f47249c62.source_title: CCUSA spreads hope with national advertising campaign

55dda4e936557c28.claim: CCUSA runs digital coordination infrastructure for the network: a Disaster Vulnerability Portal and Map giving agencies real-time disaster information, the CCConnect digital staff community, and a hub-and-spoke warehouse system for pre-staging food and disaster supplies.
55dda4e936557c28.source_title: Called to Serve: Catholic Charities USA 2025 Annual Report

b54c520e406f883d.claim: In July 2026, CCUSA published 'The Promise of Place', a white paper promoting conversion of surplus church property (closed parishes, convents, schools) into affordable housing and recommending 'Yes in God's Backyard' zoning reforms. A federal Yes in God's Backyard Act was introduced in the House in January 2026.
b54c520e406f883d.source_title: The Promise of Place (CCUSA white paper)

90dcb0a4df38a826.claim: CCUSA formally warned in July 2026 that OMB's proposed government-wide 'Regulation for Federal Financial Assistance' (91 FR 32198, May 29, 2026) could significantly increase the burden of administering federal grants and threaten agencies' planning, workforce stability and service continuity. Analyst note: if finalized as proposed, it is a structural risk to member agencies' federal partnerships.
90dcb0a4df38a826.source_title: CCUSA comments on federal financial assistance proposal

7a4e21e516be240f.claim: Rising food costs, USDA food-program cuts and a temporary loss of SNAP benefits drove a surge in pantry demand. CCUSA ran an emergency appeal in November 2025 that supplied 2.5 million pounds of food to 125 agencies in 45 states. This shows strain on capacity and also a capacity to mobilize.
7a4e21e516be240f.source_title: Called to Serve: Catholic Charities USA 2025 Annual Report

fbb071e55391aa7c.claim: Federal partnerships continue in narrower forms. Under an HHS Office of Refugee Resettlement Preferred Communities grant, 23 agencies provide intensive case management to especially vulnerable refugees and trafficking victims. CCUSA also hosts AmeriCorps VISTA members.
fbb071e55391aa7c.source_title: Called to Serve: Catholic Charities USA 2025 Annual Report

48f75380f6d0bb87.claim: CCUSA is a member of Caritas Internationalis, the worldwide federation of Catholic social-service organizations, which links it to the global Church's charitable network. Its operations are domestic, covering the 50 states, D.C. and five territories.

532ce43d19beb473.claim: Analyst judgment: Charity Navigator lists CCUSA (EIN 53-0196620) as 'Not Rated' because it has not received the required electronically filed Form 990s, and ProPublica shows no recent extracted 990 data. CCUSA does publish audited summary financials and its federal single audits are public. Third-party financial transparency is therefore limited but not absent.
532ce43d19beb473.source_title: Catholic Charities USA | Charity Navigator Profile

0b6c8f53db4caa36.claim: On June 25, 2026, after Supreme Court rulings on humanitarian protections and asylum, CCUSA called on Congress and the administration to create legal immigration pathways through bipartisan reform, while committing the network to continue humanitarian aid.
0b6c8f53db4caa36.source_title: CCUSA calls on Congress to reform immigration pathways
